summary_en: The study compares velzatinib with imatinib, the standard treatment, in adults with previously untreated gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) that have spread or cannot be surgically removed. The method of giving each drug and how long or how often it is given are not stated. The study aims to see whether velzatinib can delay disease worsening and is safe and well tolerated, but the main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 3 study.
summary_es: El estudio compara velzatinib con imatinib, el tratamiento estándar, en adultos con tumores del estroma gastrointestinal (GIST) sin tratamiento previo que se han diseminado o no se pueden extirpar con cirugía. La forma de administrar cada medicamento y con qué duración o frecuencia se dan no se indica. El estudio busca saber si velzatinib puede retrasar el empeoramiento de la enfermedad y si es seguro y bien tolerado, pero la medida principal de resultado no se indica; es un estudio de Fase 3.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older, or the legal age of consent where the study takes place.
GIST that is metastatic and/or surgically unresectable, confirmed by biopsy or cytology.
No prior systemic therapy for the metastatic or unresectable GIST.
Tumor tissue can be provided to the central laboratory.
At least one target lesion, with ECOG performance status of 1 or less.
not_for: Another malignancy that progressed or needed active treatment within the past 24 months, with listed exceptions.
Clinically significant GI problems that may alter absorption, or major stomach or bowel resection.
Major surgery within 14 days before the first dose of study treatment.
Untreated or progressing brain or central nervous system metastases.
Clinically significant cardiac disease within 6 months, QTc over 480 ms, or long QT syndrome.
